tickets.title: Equal Width Columns
tickets.description: Builds a 3-column layout where each column takes up exactly one-third of the container space on all screen sizes.
tasks: Builds a 3-column layout where each column takes up exactly one-third of the container space on all screen sizes.
tickets.evaluation: `check_class_used("container")` `check_class_used("row")` `check_class_used("col")` **[A] Visual (40 pts)**: 40 pts if layout splits into 3 equal parts. **[B] Logic (40 pts)**: 40 pts for using exactly three `.col` classes inside a `.row`. **[C] Quality (10 pts)**: 10 pts for clean semantic div nesting.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to wrap .col elements in a .container and .row.
Using col-12 on desktop instead of a specific breakpoint like col-md-4.
hints: Remember that Bootstrap uses a 12-column grid system.
Make sure columns are wrapped inside a .row class.

tickets.title: Responsive Grid Breakpoints
tickets.description: Creates a product gallery that displays 1 item per row on mobile, 2 on tablets, and 4 on desktops.
tasks: Creates a product gallery that displays 1 item per row on mobile, 2 on tablets, and 4 on desktops.
learning_objectives: Build components without relying on custom CSS.
tickets.evaluation: `check_class_used("col-12")` `check_class_used("col-md-6")` `check_class_used("col-lg-3")` **[A] Visual (40 pts)**: 40 pts if headless browser resizing triggers correct stacking. **[B] Logic (40 pts)**: 40 pts for correct breakpoint syntax. **[C] Quality (10 pts)**: 10 pts for consistent margin bottoms (`mb-4`).
common_mistakes: Writing custom CSS for things Bootstrap utilities can already do (e.g. margin, padding).
hints: Make sure you are using exact Bootstrap utility classes instead of inline styles.
Use browser developer tools to inspect elements.
